etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English schameful, schamfull, from Old English *sċeamfull, sċeomfull, equivalent to shame +‎ -ful. Cognate with Danish skamfuld (“shameful, shamefast, ashamed”).

definitions.definition: Causing or meriting shame or disgrace; disgraceful

quote.citation: 2009 February 19, Gareth Lewis, Southern Daily Echo‎[1]:
quote.text: "They have turned a great old English institution into a shameful clip-joint. It's a shuddering, howling tragedy."
